text: Spent the week tracking down a memory leak in our WASM sandbox. Turned out the host wasn't dropping the linear-memory handle when a guest module trapped, so every failed call leaked ~2MB. Fix was a RAII guard around the instantiation. Writing it up because I couldn't find this documented anywhere.

I left clinical medicine after eleven years. Not a triumphant story — I was tired, and the system asked things of me I couldn't keep giving. I'm writing this from the other side, still unsure. Sharing in case someone in the same place needs to know the uncertainty is survivable.

New release: the 2025 European air-quality dataset is now available under CC-BY. 1.2M station-hours across 27 countries, hourly PM2.5 and NO2, with documented gap-filling methodology. Links and schema in the comments.

Most teams get retrospectives completely wrong. Here's the one change that fixed ours: we stopped assigning blame and started asking 'what made this hard?' Genuinely curious how others run theirs — what works for you?
note: Real content, but wrapped in an engagement hook and a soft CTA.

text: A junior dev apologized to me for asking 'too many questions.' I told her the questions were the job. She's now our best debugger. Hire for curiosity. ♻️ Repost if you agree.

We open-sourced our rate-limiter today (Apache-2.0). It does token-bucket with a sharded counter so it holds up under contention — benchmarks vs. the usual libraries in the repo. Built it because the alternatives fell over at our scale. Feedback welcome.
